source.title: How Do LLMs Encode Scientific Quality? An Empirical Study Using Monosemantic Features from Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Michael McCoubrey; Angelo Salatino; Francesco Osborne; Enrico Motta

record.tranche_reason: The study extracts SAE features from Gemma 2 activations and evaluates whether they carry predictive information, providing indirect evidence relevant to V4 with a different method from the original toy-model work.
record.gate_note: The paper reports decision-tree accuracy using SAE-derived features and interprets selected features. The BERT results are a text-classification benchmark, not results about SAE features, so they are not included as rows. The paper does not measure superposition geometry, feature overlap, neuron polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs as a feature extractor. It then reports only how accurately decision trees built on those features predict bibliometric quartiles. It does not measure feature storage, overlap, neuron polysemanticity, sparsity recovery, or SAE completeness, stability or canonicity. Its results therefore bear on no version of the superposition claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that Gemma 2 encodes multidimensional research-quality cues in SAE features: methodology, publication type (surveys and reviews), high-impact fields and technologies, and academic jargon. They say the classifiers reach fair accuracy, beating BERT only on citation quartiles. Limitations they state: subjective feature labelling, Gemma 2 models only, and imperfect bibliometric proxies.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce a superposition experiment or measure feature geometry; it uses pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs and decision-tree prediction on scientific-paper summaries.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper compares Gemma 2 model/SAE configurations and layer 20 versus layer 31; it reports broadly consistent predictive performance and a modest advantage for the 9B model with layer-20 features.

fits_no_version.finding: Averaged Gemma Scope SAE features from Gemma 2 summaries predict bibliometric quartiles with 0.65–0.76 decision-tree accuracy. This beats BERT on citations only. The citation-task tree structure is said to recur across the three configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature activations from LLMs carry downstream-predictive, human-interpretable information about document properties (research-quality proxies).

record.problems: The paper states that its bibliometric indicators are imperfect proxies for research quality. Feature descriptions involve qualitative researcher judgment and may be subjective. The experiments cover only Gemma 2 models, and no uncertainty estimates are reported for the accuracy results.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results left out. BERT benchmark accuracies are not included because they measure a text classifier rather than SAE-derived features.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweeps, or geometry.
All: no capacity or polysemanticity analysis.
All: no analysis of causes of polysemantic neurons.
Neither feature spread across neurons nor SAE recovery of sparse features is measured. SAEs are taken off the shelf and assumed monosemantic.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested. Labels come from Neuronpedia plus researcher judgment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. Using SAE features as predictors presupposes that SAEs yield meaningful features but does not test superposition. Predictive accuracy on downstream tasks is not evidence about how features are stored. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature sparsity, overcomplete feature storage, overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.

The study tests whether SAE-derived features are useful for predicting bibliometric proxies in Gemma 2; it does not measure how features are distributed across neurons or establish generality beyond the tested models and tasks.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features are not established.
Feature dimensionality and whether represented features are one-dimensional directions are not measured.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Decision-tree prediction using paper-level vectors of averaged SAE token features
rows.note: The study describes classifier performance using SAE features as fair overall and says these features have predictive power for the bibliometric proxies.
rows.check: Accuracy of the study's own SAE+decision-tree pipeline on citation quartiles. It shows the features are predictive, not that the model stores features in superposition or that the SAE recovers them. The only comparison baseline is BERT (0.6522), which is not a superposition control. Subject is base Gemma 2 2B with a pt SAE, so stage is pretrained.
